label: While the human soul is united to the body… attacks For every being x and principle r, if the…
note: Candidate counterexample from SCG II.80 n.13 (claim AQUINAS-SCG-II-80-UNITED-SOUL-ESSE-RECEIVED-BY-BODY). Take x = a human soul united to the body and r = the body. If that is EsseReceivedIn x r in the sense of DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN (receiving potency to received act), then the premise forces the body to be the soul's essence. Aquinas denies this: the soul is a form whose esse does not depend on matter. So the premise would be false of the united soul. Whether it is a real counterexample depends on the sense of 'recipiens'. (a) Same sense: the body is in potency to the soul's esse as to its act. ST I q.76 a.1 ad 5 (passage AQUINAS-ST-I-Q76-A1, read) says the soul 'illud esse in quo ipsa subsistit, communicat materiae corporali', so corporeal matter does receive the soul's own esse. On this reading the attack holds, and the premise's 'every principle in which x's esse is received' must be restricted, for example to the principle in which x's esse is received as x's own, or to subsistent beings not united to matter. (b) Changing the bearer does not avoid the attack. If x is the composite human being, the premise still requires the receiving matter to be the composite's entire essence, which it is not. And ad 5 continues 'ita quod illud esse quod est totius compositi, est etiam ipsius animae': one esse belongs to both, not a different act borne only by the composite. The objection fails only if communicating a subsisting form's esse to matter is not EsseReceivedIn at all, a distinction now recorded as open in DISAMB-ESSE-RECEPTION. Only under that distinction is there no counterexample. (c) Restricted scope: the sentence concerns only the soul 'dum est corpori unita', so a separated soul or a pure intelligence is not attacked. Recorded as an objection, not a refutation: the reading choice is open, and nothing in Lean encodes it. A refutation would need the soul, the body and their esse typed in the EsseReceivedIn vocabulary under reading (a), with the body shown distinct from the soul's essence. Later conditional encoding: UNITED-COMMUNICATION-TO-SELECTED-RECEPTION and UNITED-RECEPTION-DEFEATS-BROAD-OWN-ESSENCE expose all those interpretation/union/act/distinctness inputs, without assigning them to this source claim. The old infinity target needs only the identity-scoped own-essence sibling; its separate strictness control preserves a nonidentity body-communication counterexample. The original source statement remains broader and unbound.
